subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser SSRF middle mode for private-network access, and if so should the first supported shape be allowlist/blocklist, interactive per-request approval, a temporary CLI grant, or no new core surface?
rationale: This changes a security boundary and public config/CLI semantics; automation should not invent approval, timeout, hard-block, logging, and upgrade behavior for private-network browser access.

options.title: Start with explicit allowlist/blocklist
options.body: Add a narrow operator-configured policy first, keep strict defaults, and require a separate reviewed design before interactive prompts or temporary grants.

options.title: Design full interactive approval
options.body: Proceed only after maintainers specify prompt routing, timeout, audit, rate-limit, redirect, and non-overridable cloud metadata behavior.

options.title: Do not add core surface
options.body: Keep current strict/broad-opt-in behavior and route homelab convenience to existing hostname exceptions or docs instead of adding another security knob.

recommendation.title: Start with explicit allowlist/blocklist
recommendation.body: Add a narrow operator-configured policy first, keep strict defaults, and require a separate reviewed design before interactive prompts or temporary grants.

likelyOwner.reason: The browser SSRF hardening and current policy shape trace most strongly to Peter Steinberger's commits.
